sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: The holiday season is a time of giving to our friends and loved ones,
sentences.zh: 假日季是一个向朋友和挚爱之人表达给予的时刻，

sentences.en: but also to strangers in the form of donations or charity.
sentences.zh: 同时也是通过捐款或慈善向陌生人伸出援手的时刻。

sentences.en: On this week's episode, we'll explore the psychology of giving.
sentences.zh: 在本周的节目中，我们将探讨给予的心理学。

sentences.en: We'll look at what motivates us to give to charities.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨是什么动机促使我们向慈善机构捐款。

sentences.en: Once they see that there's a solicitor at the door,
sentences.zh: 一旦他们看到门外有募捐者，

sentences.en: they say, oh my God, I wish I would have stayed on the couch watching the football game.
sentences.zh: 他们就会说，天哪，我真希望当时能一直躺在沙发上看球赛。

sentences.en: Why it's okay to be a re-gifter and why sometimes lying to small children can be a gift.
sentences.zh: 为什么当个“转送礼品者”没问题，以及为什么有时对小孩子撒谎也是一种礼物。

sentences.en: Fair point, but I just think you've totally lost our 8 and under demographic.
sentences.zh: 有道理，但我只是觉得你完全失去了我们8岁及以下的受众群体。

sentences.en: Finally, well-known philanthropist Adam Cole is back.
sentences.zh: 最后，知名慈善家亚当·科尔又回来了。

sentences.en: He's going to give us the gift of music and tie the episode together with a song.
sentences.zh: 他将为我们带来音乐的礼物，并用一首歌将整期节目串联起来。

sentences.en: Inspired by those really cheesy Christmas specials
sentences.zh: 灵感来自于那些非常老套的圣诞特辑，

sentences.en: in which children dance around in brightly colored sweaters.
sentences.zh: 孩子们在其中穿着色彩鲜艳的毛衣翩翩起舞。

sentences.en: Lots of us make charitable donations over the holiday season.
sentences.zh: 我们很多人在假日季都会进行慈善捐款。

sentences.en: Maybe you write a few checks.
sentences.zh: 也许你开出几张支票。

sentences.en: Maybe you donate online.
sentences.zh: 也许你在网上捐款。

sentences.en: Or maybe you get asked directly at a shopping mall
sentences.zh: 或者也许你在购物中心被直接询问，

sentences.en: or the grocery store.
sentences.zh: 或者在杂货店。

sentences.en: But what motivates you to give?
sentences.zh: 但究竟是什么动机促使你给予？

sentences.en: And does it change with the situation?
sentences.zh: 而且它会随情况而改变吗？

sentences.en: One of our producers, Maggie Penman,
sentences.zh: 我们的制作人之一玛吉·彭曼，

sentences.en: and our news assistant, Max Nestrack, went to investigate.
sentences.zh: 以及我们的新闻助理马克斯·内斯特拉克去进行了调查。

sentences.en: So Max and I went to The Giant in Silver Spring, Maryland.
sentences.zh: 所以马克斯和我去了马里兰州银泉市的吉安超市。

sentences.en: It's a big suburban grocery store, very busy on a Saturday afternoon.
sentences.zh: 那是一家大型郊区杂货店，星期六下午非常热闹。

sentences.en: But we came not to shop, but for another reason.
sentences.zh: 但我们来不是为了购物，而是为了另一个原因。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We waited in front of the Salvation Army collection.
sentences.zh: 我们在救世军募捐点前等待着。

sentences.en: We met a nice woman there named Lisa Ingram with a Santa hat on that said naughty.
sentences.zh: 我们在那儿遇到了一位名叫丽莎·英格拉姆的好心女士，她戴着一顶写着“淘气”的圣诞帽。

sentences.en: She was ringing her bell, and people were dropping in their loose change,
sentences.zh: 她在摇着铃铛，人们把零钱投进去，

sentences.en: a few dollar bills.
sentences.zh: 还有几张纸币。

sentences.en: I saw someone put a 10 in.
sentences.zh: 我看到有人塞了一张10块的进去。

sentences.en: We really wanted to know why.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很想知道为什么。

sentences.en: And the first person we talked to was Charles J.
sentences.zh: 我们采访的第一个人是小查尔斯·J·

sentences.en: Barber, Jr.
sentences.zh: 巴伯。

sentences.en: He seemed like a really popular guy.
sentences.zh: 他看起来是个很受欢迎的人。

sentences.en: Even in our very short interview,
sentences.zh: 即使在我们非常短暂的采访中，

sentences.en: he kept getting interrupted by his friends walking by.
sentences.zh: 他也不断被路过的朋友打断。

sentences.en: But he said for him, it's about being able to empathize with people who are in need.
sentences.zh: 但他说，对他而言，这关乎能够对处于困境中的人们感同身受。

sentences.en: Some of us are just a stone's throw away from being in a bad place, too.
sentences.zh: 我们中的一些人距离陷入困境也只有一步之遥。

sentences.en: So hopefully this helps people who need it.
sentences.zh: 所以希望这能帮助到需要它的人。

sentences.en: Next, there was Jarrell Becton.
sentences.zh: 接下来是贾雷尔·贝克顿。

sentences.en: I mean, it was extra change that I had.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是我身上多余的零钱。

sentences.en: I mean, every little bit counts.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，聚沙成塔。

sentences.en: I mean, every penny counts.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，积少成多。

sentences.en: Whatever you can do, just be able to reach out and help.
sentences.zh: 无论你能做什么，只要能伸出援手去帮助就行。

sentences.en: Stella Lohr was at the store with a friend.
sentences.zh: 斯特拉·洛尔和一位朋友在店里。

sentences.en: She bought me some tea that cost almost $4 or so.
sentences.zh: 她给我买了一些茶，花了我差不多4美元左右。

sentences.en: I said, well, I'll just say $4.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，我就算它是4美元吧。

sentences.en: Pay it forward.
sentences.zh: 传递爱心。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I'm just going to pay it forward.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是要把这份爱心传递下去。

sentences.en: Next, we talked to Lee Scheniger.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们采访了李·舍尼格。

sentences.en: I just give in general.
sentences.zh: 我只是习惯性地捐助。

sentences.en: I didn't lose change.
sentences.zh: 我没有丢零钱。

sentences.en: It's simply that.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这么简单。

sentences.en: Does it make you feel good when you give?
sentences.zh: 当你给予的时候，这会让你感觉良好吗？

sentences.en: Oh, I suppose so.
sentences.zh: 哦，我想是的。

sentences.en: And finally, we talked to Bonnie Scott.
sentences.zh: 最后，我们采访了邦妮·斯科特。

sentences.en: So why did you put a dollar in the bucket?
sentences.zh: 那你为什么往桶里放了一美元呢？

sentences.en: Well, I like to see people being helped.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我喜欢看到人们得到帮助。

sentences.en: So why not give them a dollar when I see them?
sentences.zh: 所以当我看到他们时，为什么不给他们一美元呢？

sentences.en: Do you give every time you see the Salvation Army bucket?
sentences.zh: 每次看到救世军的募捐桶你都会捐吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I'm guilty.
sentences.zh: 我有罪（我承认）。

sentences.en: And why do you think you always have to, like, every time you go to the store around this
sentences.zh: 那你为什么觉得你总是必须，比如说，每到一年中的这个时候去店里，

sentences.en: time of year, why do you feel like you have to give a dollar?
sentences.zh: 为什么你觉得你必须捐出一美元？

sentences.en: People need right now.
sentences.zh: 人们现在就需要帮助。

sentences.en: So why not?
sentences.zh: 所以为什么不呢？

sentences.en: So there you have it, Scheniger.
sentences.zh: 所以，就是这样，舍尼格。

sentences.en: People give because they want to help.
sentences.zh: 人们给予是因为他们想帮忙。

sentences.en: Because it makes them feel good.
sentences.zh: 因为这让他们感觉良好。

sentences.en: And because they want to pay it forward.
sentences.zh: 并且因为他们想传递爱心。

sentences.en: That was Maggie Penman and Max Nestrack with a lot of very sweet people at the grocery
sentences.zh: 那是玛吉·彭曼和马克斯·内斯特拉克在杂货店里采访了许多非常善良的人，

sentences.en: store showing us the positive side of generosity.
sentences.zh: 向我们展示了慷慨积极的一面。

sentences.en: But there's also a more cynical take.
sentences.zh: 但也有更具讽刺意味的看法。

sentences.en: And that was summarized in a recent episode of South Park, where Stan's dad, Randy Marsh,
sentences.zh: 这在最近一集《南方公园》中被精辟地总结了，斯坦的爸爸兰迪·马什，

sentences.en: gets pressured to donate a dollar at the checkout line at a very socially conscious Whole Foods.
sentences.zh: 在一家极具社会责任感的全食超市结账时，被迫捐出一美元。

sentences.en: Okay, sir.
sentences.zh: 好的，先生。

sentences.en: Looks like your total is $37.83.
sentences.zh: 您的总额是37.83美元。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 行。

sentences.en: And would you like to add a dollar donation to help hungry kids around the world?
sentences.zh: 您愿意额外捐款一美元来帮助世界各地饥饿的儿童吗？

sentences.en: Oh, uh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，呃，不用了。

sentences.en: That's okay.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: Sorry?
sentences.zh: 抱歉？

sentences.en: I'm good.
sentences.zh: 我不用了。

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: You don't want to give the dollar to hungry kids?
sentences.zh: 你不想把这一美元给饥饿的儿童吗？

sentences.en: Not today.
sentences.zh: 今天不。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: No problem.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: Window's going to come up and ask if you're helping the hungry kids.
sentences.zh: 屏幕将会弹出来询问你是否在帮助饥饿的儿童。

sentences.en: Just hit, no, I'm not.
sentences.zh: 直接点击“不，我没有”。

sentences.en: Oh, come on.
sentences.zh: 哦，拜托。

sentences.en: Try hitting it again.
sentences.zh: 再试着点一下。

sentences.en: It's the box below the one that says, sure, I'd love to help however I can.
sentences.zh: 就是写着“当然，我很乐意尽我所能提供帮助”下面那个方框。

sentences.en: Ah, darn thing.
sentences.zh: 啊，该死的东西。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: Most people give the dollar.
sentences.zh: 大多数人都捐了一美元。

sentences.en: I can do this manually.
sentences.zh: 我可以手动操作这个。

sentences.en: Look, I give money to charity a lot, okay?
sentences.zh: 听着，我经常向慈善机构捐款，好吗？

sentences.en: Oh, sure you do.
sentences.zh: 哦，你当然捐了。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我真的捐。

sentences.en: I just don't want to every time I shop for food.
sentences.zh: 我只是不想每次买食物时都捐。

sentences.en: That's completely understandable.
sentences.zh: 这完全可以理解。

sentences.en: Have customers speak.
sentences.zh: 请顾客发言。

sentences.en: Oh, if you can just speak into the voice decoder and say, I'm not giving anything to the hungry
sentences.zh: 哦，如果你能对着语音解码器说“我不会给饥饿的儿童任何东西”，

sentences.en: kids.
sentences.zh: 就行了。

sentences.en: I'm not giving anything to the hungry kids.
sentences.zh: 我不会给饥饿的儿童任何东西。

sentences.en: So which version of generosity is right?
sentences.zh: 那么哪一种版本的慷慨才是正确的？

sentences.en: The positive, life-affirming people that Maggie and Max talked with, or the guilt-tripped
sentences.zh: 是玛吉和马克斯交谈过的那些积极、肯定生活的人，还是结账时被道德绑架的慈善家？

sentences.en: philanthropist at the checkout line?
sentences.zh: 我最近与《译言堂》（All Things Considered）的主持人奥迪·康尼斯就此进行了对话。

sentences.en: I recently had a conversation about this with All Things Considered host Audie Cornish.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论了为什么你认为自己捐款的原因可能并不是真正的原因。

sentences.en: We talked about why the reasons you think you give may not actually be the real reason.
sentences.zh: 所以正如他们所说，在每年的这个时候，人们被认为更有慈善心。

sentences.en: So this is the time of year, as they say, when people are perceived as being more charitable.
sentences.zh: 但这一切都是出于利他主义吗？

sentences.en: But is it all altruistic?
sentences.zh: 好吧，当你问人们为什么慷慨时，他们会告诉你这完全是出于利他主义，

sentences.en: Well, when you ask people why they are generous, they will tell you that it is all about altruism,
sentences.zh: 他们热爱某个事业或者他们喜欢给予。

sentences.en: that they love a cause or they like to give.
sentences.zh: 但科学家们越来越多地试图检验这些说法，奥迪。

sentences.en: But scientists have increasingly sought to test these claims, Audie.
sentences.zh: 我采访了经济学家约翰·李斯特。

sentences.en: I spoke with economist John LiSt.
sentences.zh: 他在芝加哥大学。

sentences.en: He's at the University of Chicago.
sentences.zh: 他做过许多关于人们为什么捐款的实验。

sentences.en: He's conducted a number of experiments into why people give.
sentences.zh: 他向我解释了为什么他认为这样做很重要。

sentences.en: And he explained to me why he thinks this is important to do.
sentences.zh: 每当你问某人，你为什么要给这个慈善事业捐款？

sentences.en: Anytime you ask someone, why did you give to this charitable cause?
sentences.zh: 典型的回答是，我捐款是因为我真的很想帮助另一个人。

sentences.en: The typical response is, I gave because I really want to help another person.
sentences.zh: 但当你真正深入挖掘时，那并不是他们捐款的真正动机。

sentences.en: But when you actually dig down deeper, that's not the true motive for why they gave.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们需要实地实验来试图厘清人们捐款原因的原因。

sentences.en: And that's exactly why we need field experiments to try to disentangle reasons why people give.
sentences.zh: 我明白，查克，其中一个原因可能是社会压力，对吧？

sentences.en: And I understand, Chuck, one of the reasons may be social pressure, right?
sentences.zh: 而他做了一些实验来试图证明这一点。

sentences.en: And he does some experiments to try and make that case.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 所以李斯特认为社会压力可能扮演了非常强大的角色。

sentences.en: So List thinks that social pressure might be playing a very powerful role.
sentences.zh: 他让我思考一个我们很多人都会感到熟悉的场景。

sentences.en: And he asked me to think about a scenario that's going to be familiar to lots of us.
sentences.zh: 他又来了。

sentences.en: Here he is again.
sentences.zh: 你正坐在沙发上看球赛。

sentences.en: You're sitting on the couch watching a football game.
sentences.zh: 然后你听到有人在敲门。

sentences.en: And you hear somebody knocking on the door.
sentences.zh: 你心想，好吧，我是该起来开门还是继续看球赛？

sentences.en: And you think, OK, should I get up or should I stay watching the football game?
sentences.zh: 当然，很多人都会起来去开门。

sentences.en: Of course, a lot of people get up and answer the door.
sentences.zh: 但一旦他们看到门外有募捐者，他们就会说：

sentences.en: But once they see that there's a solicitor at the door, they say,
sentences.zh: “哦，天哪，我真希望当时能一直躺在沙发上看球赛。”

sentences.en: Oh, my God, I wish I would have stayed on the couch watching the football game.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，你觉得自己被架在火上烤了。

sentences.en: So basically, you feel like you've been put on the spot.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 李斯特意识到，这个场景为一项实验提供了完美的机制，该实验试图弄清楚社会压力在利他主义中起到了多大作用。

sentences.en: And List realized that this scenario provides the perfect mechanism for an experiment that tries to find out how much social pressure plays a role in altruism.
sentences.zh: 李斯特派志愿者到芝加哥的各个社区为一家儿童医院募捐。

sentences.en: List sent volunteers into various Chicago neighborhoods to solicit money for a children's hospital.
sentences.zh: 但有个附加条件，奥迪。

sentences.en: But there was a catch, Adi.
sentences.zh: 有些住户只是接到了一通突击拜访，也就是敲门募捐。

sentences.en: Some households just got a cold call, a knock on the door.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则提前收到通知，知道有人会来敲门并索要捐款。

sentences.en: Others were alerted ahead of time that someone was going to be knocking on their door and asking for money.
sentences.zh: 第三组被告知敲门即将到来，并被赋予了选择退出的权利。

sentences.en: A third group was told that a knock was coming and given the choice to opt out.
sentences.zh: 第三组被告知将会有敲门声，并可选择退出。

sentences.en: They could say they didn't want to be disturbed.
sentences.zh: 他们可以说自己不想被打扰。

sentences.en: Now, if people were giving only because of altruism, it shouldn't matter whether they know ahead of time that a knock is coming.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果人们捐款纯粹是为了利他，那么他们是否提前知道有人来敲门应该并不重要。

sentences.en: But List finds that when households are alerted ahead of time, the number of people who answer that knock on the door, it falls by a quarter.
sentences.zh: 但利斯特发现，当住户提前接到通知时，开门应答的人数会下降四分之一。

sentences.en: When people are given the choice to opt out and say they don't want to be disturbed, donations fall by nearly half.
sentences.zh: 当人们可以选择退出并表示不想被打扰时，捐款额会下降近一半。

sentences.en: And what List says to show is how much social pressure shapes generosity.
sentences.zh: 利斯特以此来表明社会压力对慷慨程度的影响有多大。

sentences.en: What you find is that roughly three quarters of the dollars given are due to social pressure and a quarter of the dollars given is actually due to altruism.
sentences.zh: 你发现大约四分之三的捐款是由于社会压力，而四分之一的捐款实际上是由于利他主义。

sentences.en: Now, of course, Adi, we should mention that this was one experiment in one setting.
sentences.zh: 当然，阿迪，我们应该提到这只是特定环境下的一个实验。

sentences.en: There are lots of other reasons why people might want to give.
sentences.zh: 人们想要捐款的原因还有很多。

sentences.en: People write checks in the privacy of their own homes where there's no social pressure.
sentences.zh: 人们在自己私密的家中开支票，那里没有社会压力。

sentences.en: But in this kind of situation, and there are many like it, you know, you encounter somebody at the door of a store as you're leaving,
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下——而且有很多类似的情况，你知道的，当你离开时在商店门口遇到某人，

sentences.en: or maybe you're at church and people are passing the collection plate.
sentences.zh: 或者也许你在教堂里，人们正在传递奉献盘。

sentences.en: It's situations like that where social pressure probably plays an enormous role.
sentences.zh: 正是在这种情况下，社会压力可能扮演了极其重要的角色。

sentences.en: So the idea that you're basically uncomfortable saying no to someone's face, right?
sentences.zh: 所以那种基本上不好意思当面拒绝别人的感觉，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So in this experiment, you don't want the person at the door to think that you're a jerk for not wanting to help a children's hospital.
sentences.zh: 所以在这次实验中，你不想让门口的人觉得你因为不想资助儿童医院而是个混蛋。

sentences.en: The dilemma, Adi, is that for charities, putting people on the spot is effective,
sentences.zh: 阿迪，两难之处在于，对于慈善机构来说，把人架在火上烤很有效，

sentences.en: but it might be effective only in the short term because people don't like to be pressured and they're going to find ways to dodge it.
sentences.zh: 但它可能只在短期内有效，因为人们不喜欢被施压，他们会想方设法躲避。

sentences.en: List, in fact,
sentences.zh: 事实上，利斯特

sentences.en: believes that charities need to focus on the 25% of people who are genuinely motivated by altruism because this is the group of people who are likely to be your long-term supporters.
sentences.zh: 认为慈善机构需要关注那25%真正出于利他动机的人，因为这群人很可能成为你的长期支持者。

sentences.en: So what are some of the other strategies that charities and others have found to get us to open our wallets?
sentences.zh: 那么，慈善机构和其他组织为了让我们打开钱包，还发现了哪些其他策略？

sentences.en: You know, Adi, there are literally dozens of different things that people have tried.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，阿迪，人们尝试过的方法简直有几十种之多。

sentences.en: One of them is that when a charity sends you a gift, maybe they send you a calendar, the norm of reciprocity dictates that you send something back to them in exchange.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是，当慈善机构给你送礼物时，比如送你一本台历，互惠规范会要求你回赠他们一些东西。

sentences.en: Another idea is that if you can get people to donate their time to a cause, they're more likely to follow up with donations because people's wallets follow their feet.
sentences.zh: 另一个想法是，如果你能让人们为一项事业贡献时间，他们更有可能会用捐款来跟进，因为人们的钱包跟着他们的双脚走。

sentences.en: So I'm feeling a little guilty now for my introduction, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我现在对我的开场白感到有点内疚，对吧？

sentences.en: The norms of the holiday season, right?
sentences.zh: 节日季的规范，对吧？

sentences.en: This is the time of year to give.
sentences.zh: 这是一年中送礼的时刻。

sentences.en: Does that also create a form of social pressure?
sentences.zh: 这也会产生一种社会压力吗？

sentences.en: You can think about social norms exactly as a larger example of social pressure at work.
sentences.zh: 你可以把社会规范看作是社会压力在起作用的一个更大范例。

sentences.en: If you're at a workplace and everyone's writing checks to charities or doing things that are charitable, you feel kind of obliged to do the same.
sentences.zh: 如果你在职场中，每个人都在给慈善机构开支票或者做慈善活动，你就会觉得有义务做同样的事。

sentences.en: Shankar, thanks so much for explaining it.
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，非常感谢你的解释。

sentences.en: Thank you so much, Adi.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你，阿迪。

sentences.en: After this short break, Dan Pink is back for another round of Stopwatch Science.
sentences.zh: 这段简短的休息之后，丹·平克将带着又一轮“秒表科学”节目回归。

sentences.en: We'll give you some tips on how to be more generous and give better gifts.
sentences.zh: 我们将为你提供一些关于如何变得更慷慨以及送出更好礼物的建议。

sentences.en: We'll also tell you about the downside of altruism.
sentences.zh: 我们还会告诉你利他主义的负面影响。

sentences.en: After this.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来。

sentences.en: Welcome back.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回来。

sentences.en: We have more ideas about charity and gift giving in our next Stopwatch Science segment.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的“秒表科学”环节中，我们有更多关于慈善和送礼的想法。

sentences.en: I'm joined as usual by senior Stopwatch Science correspondent, Daniel Pink.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样，陪伴我的是“秒表科学”资深记者丹尼尔·平克。

sentences.en: Hi, Dan.
sentences.zh: 嗨，丹。

sentences.en: Hey, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 嘿，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: As we've heard in the previous segment, altruism is a complicated thing.
sentences.zh: 正如我们在上一环节中所听到的，利他主义是一件复杂的事情。

sentences.en: It makes people feel warm and happy, but it's also driven by social pressure and public norMs.
sentences.zh: 它让人感到温暖和快乐，但它也受到社会压力和公众规范的驱动。

sentences.en: On this edition of Stopwatch Science, Dan and I will present two ideas each from social science research looking at the science of generosity.
sentences.zh: 在本期“秒表科学”中，丹和我将各自从社会科学研究中提出两个关于慷慨科学的想法。

sentences.en: We get 60 seconds to present each idea, and as we approach the 60-second mark, our producers will gently bring up the music like they do at the Oscars.
sentences.zh: 我们有60秒的时间来阐述每个想法，当我们接近60秒大关时，我们的制作人会像在奥斯卡颁奖典礼上那样，轻柔地响起音乐。

sentences.en: Dan, if you're ready, your first 60 seconds starts now.
sentences.zh: 丹，如果你准备好了，你的前60秒现在开始。

sentences.en: Okay, let's say you're choosing a holiday gift for a friend, and you're deciding between two video games.
sentences.zh: 好的，假设你正在为朋友挑选节日礼物，你正在两款电子游戏之间做选择。

sentences.en: Now, one game is high-end and super cool, but it takes a while to learn.
sentences.zh: 其中一款游戏高端且超级酷，但需要花一些时间来学习。

sentences.en: The other is more ordinary.
sentences.zh: 另一款则更普通一些。

sentences.en: It's easy to start playing, but the game is just medium quality and less nifty.
sentences.zh: 它很容易上手，但游戏质量只是一般，也没有那么精巧。

sentences.en: Which gift would you rather give, and which would your friend rather receive?
sentences.zh: 你更愿意送出哪件礼物，你的朋友又更想收到哪件呢？

sentences.en: Now, those questions are at the heart of a fascinating paper last year in the Journal of Consumer Research.
sentences.zh: 这些问题是去年发表在《消费者研究杂志》上一篇引人入胜的论文的核心。

sentences.en: Over eight experiments, researchers found that givers consistently chose desirability, special gifts, even if they're a hassle,
sentences.zh: 通过八项实验，研究人员发现，送礼者总是选择渴望度高、特别的礼物，即使这些礼物很麻烦，

sentences.en: like that turbocharged video game or a gift certificate to a great Italian restaurant that's an hour away.
sentences.zh: 比如那款性能强劲的电子游戏，或者一张距离一小时车程的一家棒极了的意大利餐厅的礼品卡。

sentences.en: But receivers consistently valued feasibility just as much.
sentences.zh: 但接受者对可行性的重视程度始终不相上下。

sentences.en: They were equally happy with that easy-to-play video game or a gift card to an okay Italian restaurant around the corner.
sentences.zh: 他们对那款易于游玩的电子游戏，或者转角处一家还不错的意大利餐厅的礼品卡感到同样高兴。

sentences.en: When we select gifts for people, we often aim for desirability.
sentences.zh: 当我们为人们挑选礼物时，我们常常追求渴望度。

sentences.en: We want to pick something special, unique, unforgettable.
sentences.zh: 我们想挑选一些特别的、独特的、令人难忘的东西。

sentences.en: But it turns out that the people on the receiving end, they don't much care.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，接受礼物的人并不太在意这些。

sentences.en: They're just as happy with gifts that are easy, convenient, and practical.
sentences.zh: 他们对那些简单、方便且实用的礼物同样感到高兴。

sentences.en: I love that, Dan.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢这个了，丹。

sentences.en: And I think this speaks to something that you've brought up before on Stopwatch Science,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这说明了你之前在“秒表科学”中提到过的一点，

sentences.en: which is that we are often really bad at reading other people's minds.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们常常真的不擅长猜透别人的心思。

sentences.en: We're terrible at it, and we don't know it.
sentences.zh: 我们对此一窍不通，而且我们自己还不知道。

sentences.en: So there are some workarounds that we can do.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以采取一些变通的方法。

sentences.en: For instance, Francesca Gino, who is a friend of the show, has a great paper from a few years ago
sentences.zh: 例如，节目的老朋友弗朗西斯卡·吉诺在几年前有一篇极佳的论文，

sentences.en: showing that the best way to select a gift for someone is to ask them what they want
sentences.zh: 表明为某人挑选礼物的最好方法是直接问他们想要什么，

sentences.en: rather than try to divine it through telepathy.
sentences.zh: 而不是试图通过心灵感应去猜测。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I get the message.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: Dan, what do you want for Christmas?
sentences.zh: 丹，你圣诞节想要什么？

sentences.en: Let's see.
sentences.zh: 让我想想。

sentences.en: Well, actually, my coffee maker broke, so I really just need a coffee maker pretty badly.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实我的咖啡机坏了，所以我真的很需要一台咖啡机。

sentences.en: And not a fancy one with special little valves and things that steam and wor things around,
sentences.zh: 而且不要那种带有特殊小阀门、会冒蒸汽、能把东西转来转去的花哨咖啡机，

sentences.en: just a regular working man's coffee maker.
sentences.zh: 就要一台普通实用的咖啡机。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Consider it done.
sentences.zh: 包在我身上。

sentences.en: All right, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 好的，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: Your 60 seconds starts right now.
sentences.zh: 你的60秒现在开始。

sentences.en: Many of us think that learning a musical instrument or becoming a gymnast are skills that can be learned or improved with practice.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人认为，学习乐器或成为体操运动员是通过练习可以学习或提高的技能。

sentences.en: Well, we don't think of generosity and altruism the same way.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们并不以同样的方式看待慷慨和利他主义。

sentences.en: We don't think of compassion as a skill when, in fact, there's evidence that you can train yourself to be more compassionate.
sentences.zh: 我们不认为同情心是一种技能，而事实上，有证据表明你可以通过训练让自己更有同情心。

sentences.en: Helen Wang and Richard Davidson at the University of Wisconsin at Madison, along with other researchers,
sentences.zh: 威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校的海伦·王和理查德·戴维森，以及其他研究人员，

sentences.en: they train volunteers to think kindly about others, to cultivate compassion, both for loved ones as well as for strangers.
sentences.zh: 他们训练志愿者对他人怀有善意，培养同情心，既针对挚爱之人，也针对陌生人。

sentences.en: They find in a study published in the journal Psychological Science that when you do this for 30 minutes a day for two weeks,
sentences.zh: 他们在发表在《心理科学》杂志上的一项研究中发现，当你连续两周每天进行30分钟这样的练习时，

sentences.en: volunteers become more likely to act compassionately towards strangers who are in need of help.
sentences.zh: 志愿者更有可能对需要帮助的陌生人表现出富有同情心的行为。

sentences.en: In other words, mental training alone can change your ability to respond to the suffering of others.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，单靠心理训练就能改变你对他人苦难做出反应的能力。

sentences.en: They also find, very interestingly, there's evidence using fMRI scanners that there are changes in the brain areas of volunteers who get the training.
sentences.zh: 他们还非常有意思地发现，利用功能性磁共振成像（fMRI）扫描的证据表明，接受培训的志愿者的脑区发生了变化。

sentences.en: And these brain areas include the inferior parietal cortex and the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex.
sentences.zh: 这些大脑区域包括下顶叶皮层和背外侧前额叶皮层。

sentences.en: That's fascinating and heartening.
sentences.zh: 这既迷人又令人振奋。

sentences.en: And, you know, Martin Seligman years ago wrote a book called Learned Optimism, based on his research in learned helplessness.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，马丁·塞利格曼多年前根据他对习得性无助的研究写过一本书叫《学习乐观》。

sentences.en: So what we're talking here is learned compassion, which would be, no joke, a really great gift in the holidays.
sentences.zh: 所以我们这里讨论的是习得性同情，说真的，这真的是节日里一份极好的礼物。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: And it's part of a larger body of work known as positive psychology, looking at how psychology can help us understand the best of ourselves, not just the worst of ourselves.
sentences.zh: 这是被称为积极心理学的一个更大研究体系的一部分，该体系探讨心理学如何帮助我们理解我们最好的一面，而不仅仅是最坏的一面。

sentences.en: But, Dan, I'm going to turn it over to you for your second study.
sentences.zh: 但是，丹，我要把时间交给你，让你讲第二个研究。

sentences.en: Your next 60 seconds starts right now.
sentences.zh: 你的下一个60秒现在开始。

sentences.en: Okay, here's a less exalted scenario, right?
sentences.zh: 好的，这是一个不那么崇高的场景，对吧？

sentences.en: Someone gives me a present, say a watch.
sentences.zh: 有人送我一件礼物，比如一块手表。

sentences.en: I open it and think, eh, it's not my style.
sentences.zh: 我打开一看，心想，呃，这不是我的风格。

sentences.en: So I stick it in a new box, rewrap it, and give it to my brother.
sentences.zh: 于是我把它塞进一个新的盒子里，重新包装好，送给了我弟弟。

sentences.en: It's called re-gifting.
sentences.zh: 这叫转赠礼物。

sentences.en: And it's offensive, right?
sentences.zh: 这很冒犯，对吧？

sentences.en: A social taboo.
sentences.zh: 一种社会禁忌。

sentences.en: Well, a set of studies by Gabrielle Adams at the London Business School says, maybe not.
sentences.zh: 好吧，伦敦商学院加布里埃尔·亚当斯的一系列研究表明，也许并非如此。

sentences.en: Adams and colleagues at Harvard and Stanford set up several experiments in which some people were gift givers and others were gift receivers.
sentences.zh: 亚当斯和哈佛大学及斯坦福大学的同事们设置了几个实验，其中一些人是送礼者，另一些人是收礼者。

sentences.en: Then they had some of the receivers repackage their gifts and give them to someone else.
sentences.zh: 然后他们让一些收礼者重新包装他们的礼物并送给其他人。

sentences.en: Turns out, over and over again, the re-gifters overestimated how much the givers of the original gift would be offended.
sentences.zh: 结果证明，一次又一次地，转赠者高估了原礼物赠送者被冒犯的程度。

sentences.en: They thought the givers would be shocked, hurt, appalled by the re-gifting, but most givers said, hey, it's your gift now.
sentences.zh: 他们以为赠送者会对转赠感到震惊、受伤、震惊，但大多数赠送者说，嘿，现在这礼物是你的了。

sentences.en: The title is essentially passed to you.
sentences.zh: 所有权基本上已经转交给你了。

sentences.en: Do whatever you want.
sentences.zh: 你想怎么处理都行。

sentences.en: The stigma of re-gifting wasn't much of a stigma at all.
sentences.zh: 转赠礼物的污名其实并没有那么严重。

sentences.en: Dan, I want to thank you for sanctioning my inner re-gifter.
sentences.zh: 丹，我要感谢你认可了我内心那个想要转赠礼物的人。

sentences.en: I feel completely liberated now in ways that should be very interesting to watch over the next few weeks.
sentences.zh: 我现在感到彻底解放了，这种方式在接下来的几周里应该会非常有趣。

sentences.en: That's great because I got a really special present for you.
sentences.zh: 那太好了，因为我为你准备了一份非常特别的礼物。

sentences.en: High in desirability, but really difficult to use.
sentences.zh: 渴望度很高，但真的很难使用。

sentences.en: So you just give it to somebody else and you'll feel better.
sentences.zh: 所以你把它送给别人，你就会感觉好多了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Now, your 60 seconds for your study, Shankar, starts right now.
sentences.zh: 现在，关于你的研究的60秒，尚卡尔，现在开始。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: This is also a study that looks at altruism.
sentences.zh: 这也是一项研究利他主义的研究。

sentences.en: Except, Dan, it looks at the downside of altruism.
sentences.zh: 只不过，丹，它着眼于利他主义的消极面。

sentences.en: It's a study by a friend of the show, Francesca Gino, at the Harvard Business School.
sentences.zh: 这是哈佛商学院节目老朋友弗朗西斯卡·吉诺的一项研究。

sentences.en: You just mentioned her a moment ago.
sentences.zh: 你刚才才提到过她。

sentences.en: Along with Shahar Ayal and Dan Ariely, Gino found that people are more likely to cheat when their behavior is hidden.
sentences.zh: 吉诺与沙哈尔·阿亚尔和丹·艾瑞里一起发现，当人们的行为被隐藏时，他们更有可能作弊。

sentences.en: That's not surprising.
sentences.zh: 这并不令人意外。

sentences.en: Here's the part of her study that caught my eye.
sentences.zh: 这是她研究中吸引我眼球的部分。

sentences.en: When people feel that their cheating can help another person as well as themselves, cheating goes up substantially.
sentences.zh: 当人们觉得他们的作弊不仅能帮助自己还能帮助别人时，作弊行为会大幅增加。

sentences.en: When being dishonest can help an entire group, cheating goes up even more.
sentences.zh: 当不诚实行为可以帮助整个群体时，作弊行为就会增加得更多。

sentences.en: Or what's fascinating to me here, Dan, is how the hidden brain weaves together these different motives.
sentences.zh: 对我来说最迷人的是，丹，隐藏的大脑是如何将这些不同的动机交织在一起的。

sentences.en: Wanting to help others is a good thing.
sentences.zh: 想要帮助他人是一件好事。

sentences.en: In this case, people use a positive motive to justify being dishoneSt.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，人们利用积极的动机来为不诚实的行为辩护。

sentences.en: Now, I know it's the holiday season, Dan, but I'm going to make a little editorial statement here.
sentences.zh: 现在，我知道这是节日季，丹，但我在这里要发表一点社论式的声明。

sentences.en: One of the things that many of us do is we lie to children about the existence of Santa Claus.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人做的一件事就是对孩子们撒谎，说圣诞老人存在。

sentences.en: We perpetrate this act of mass dishonesty, but we do it because we say it's in the common good.
sentences.zh: 我们犯下了这种大规模的不诚实行为，但我们这样做是因为我们说这是为了公共利益。

sentences.en: Fair point, but I just think you've totally lost our eight-and-under demographic.
sentences.zh: 有道理，但我只是觉得你彻底失去了我们八岁及以下的人口统计群体。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: There you have it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: Give gifts that are useful.
sentences.zh: 送有用的礼物。

sentences.en: Train yourself to be more compassionate.
sentences.zh: 训练自己更有同情心。

sentences.en: Beware of the downside of altruism.
sentences.zh: 小心利他主义的负面影响。

sentences.en: And re-gift shamelessly.
sentences.zh: 毫无羞耻感地转赠礼物。

sentences.en: If you get caught, tell people Dan Pink told you to do it.
sentences.zh: 如果你被抓到了，就告诉别人是丹·平克让你这么做的。

sentences.en: Dan, thank you so much for joining us.
sentences.zh: 丹，非常感谢你加入我们。

sentences.en: My pleasure, I think.
sentences.zh: 我的荣幸，我想是的。

sentences.en: That was Daniel Pink, our senior stopwatch science correspondent and ace gift giver.
sentences.zh: 那是丹尼尔·平克，我们的“秒表科学”资深记者和王牌送礼达人。

sentences.en: Can't wait to see what you got me for Christmas, Dan.
sentences.zh: 等不及看你给我买的圣诞礼物了，丹。

sentences.en: We have one last segment for you this holiday.
sentences.zh: 这个节日我们为你准备了最后一个环节。

sentences.en: Adam Cole is back to tie this episode together with a song.
sentences.zh: 亚当·科尔回归，用一首歌将这一集串联起来。

sentences.en: Adam, welcome back to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 亚当，欢迎回到“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Did you put in hours and hours of work to create this original song for us, Adam?
sentences.zh: 亚当，你是不是花了好几个小时的工作来为我们创作这首原创歌曲？

sentences.en: Well, I put in a lot of hours listening to the episode, and I put in a lot of hours listening to holiday music to get inspiration,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我花了很多时间听这期节目，也花了很多时间听节日音乐来寻找灵感，

sentences.en: since this is a holiday episode.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一期节日特别节目。

sentences.en: So, yeah, put together a little piece sort of inspired by those really cheesy Christmas specials in which children dance around in brightly colored sweaters.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我拼凑了一小段音乐，灵感正是来自那些穿着色彩鲜艳的毛衣、翩翩起舞的小朋友的俗气圣诞特别节目。

sentences.en: Wonderful.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: And did you do this all by yourself, Adam, or did you have help?
sentences.zh: 这是你自己一个人完成的，亚当，还是有人帮你？

sentences.en: Well, you know, I actually got some help from your producer, Maggie Penman.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实我得到了你们的制片人玛吉·彭曼的帮助。

sentences.en: She sings on this song.
sentences.zh: 这首歌里有她的歌声。

sentences.en: Oh, cool.
sentences.zh: 哦，酷。

sentences.en: And there's also a special guest appearance by someone you said doesn't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 而且还有一个神秘嘉宾出场，就是你曾经说根本不存在的那个人。

sentences.en: I can't wait to hear this.
sentences.zh: 我迫不及待想听听了。

sentences.en: The chestnuts are roasting, and Shankar stopped hosting, so he could go out and sled.
sentences.zh: 栗子在烘烤，香卡停下了主持，跑出去玩雪橇。

sentences.en: There's jingle bells belling, and our hearts are swelling, and Dan Pink is yelling about something he read.
sentences.zh: 铃儿在叮当响，我们的内心在澎湃，丹·平克在对读到的内容大喊大叫。

sentences.en: We're full of Christmas cheer, but let's make one thing very clear.
sentences.zh: 我们充满了节日的气氛，但有一点必须说清楚。

sentences.en: The gifts you give are thoughtful, but they're also often awful.
sentences.zh: 你们送的礼物虽然贴心，但也常常糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: Just give us what we asked for this year.
sentences.zh: 今年就给我们想要的东西吧。

sentences.en: Five-star dinner, but we'll take your coffee maker and a piece of pizza down the street.
sentences.zh: 五星级大餐就算了，但我们收下你的咖啡机和街头的一块披萨。

sentences.en: If we open a gift and we don't like what we find, we'll just re-gift it.
sentences.zh: 如果我们打开礼物不喜欢，我们就会转手送人。

sentences.en: You won't mind, but it would be terrific if you gave us the specific thing that we asked for this Christmas time.
sentences.zh: 你不会介意的，但如果你能直接送我们今年圣诞节想要的那样特定东西，那就太棒了。

sentences.en: Now hold on a minute.
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: Santa Claus?
sentences.zh: 圣诞老人？

sentences.en: Oh, yes, it's me, and I'm here to tell you, you're terrible.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，就是我，我来告诉你，你太差劲了。

sentences.en: This isn't the season of receiving, it's the season of altruism.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个接受的季节，这是一个利他主义的季节。

sentences.en: Altruism?
sentences.zh: 利他主义？

sentences.en: Sounds lame, Santa.
sentences.zh: 听起来真逊，圣诞老人。

sentences.en: Yeah, what do you know?
sentences.zh: 就是，你懂什么？

sentences.en: You're just an act of mass dishonesty we perpetrate annually for the sake of children.
sentences.zh: 你不过是一场为了孩子而每年上演的大规模骗局。

sentences.en: Oh, nonsense.
sentences.zh: 哦，胡说八道。

sentences.en: I'm the living embodiment of the spirit of giving.
sentences.zh: 我是奉献精神的活生生的化身。

sentences.en: But I wasn't always that way.
sentences.zh: 但我并不总是这样的。

sentences.en: Before my current role, way up at the North Pole,
sentences.zh: 在我扮演目前的角色之前，远在北极的时候，

sentences.en: I was a mean old elf.
sentences.zh: 我曾是一个刻薄的老精灵。

sentences.en: Oh, just like the Grinch, my heart, it was pinched,
sentences.zh: 哦，就像格林奇一样，我的心紧缩着，

sentences.en: and I only thought of myself.
sentences.zh: 我只想着自己。

sentences.en: But then I practiced caring.
sentences.zh: 但后来我练习了关怀。

sentences.en: Thirty minutes every day.
sentences.zh: 每天三十分钟。

sentences.en: And my dorsolateral prefrontal cortex slowly began to chew.
sentences.zh: 我的背外侧前额叶皮层慢慢开始活跃起来。

sentences.en: I don't know, Santa.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，圣诞老人。

sentences.en: Practicing empathy sounds like a lot of work.
sentences.zh: 练习同理心听起来像是一项繁重的工作。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: A lot of people don't practice compassion.
sentences.zh: 很多人并不练习同情心。

sentences.en: They're only generous when they think people are watching.
sentences.zh: 他们只有在觉得自己受到关注时才会慷慨。

sentences.en: That's why I watch from my sleigh both night and day
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我日夜坐在雪橇上注视着

sentences.en: A jolly one-man NSA
sentences.zh: 一个欢乐的个人国安局

sentences.en: So if someone poor is at your door
sentences.zh: 所以如果哪个穷人来到你的门前

sentences.en: I'll see if you turn them away
sentences.zh: 我会看着你是否把他们赶走

sentences.en: If you don't help people with their problems
sentences.zh: 如果你不帮别人解决问题

sentences.en: You'll make my list and not the dice column
sentences.zh: 你就会上我的黑名单，而不是好孩子名单

sentences.en: It's my duty and my pleasure to apply the social pressure
sentences.zh: 施加社会压力是我的职责和乐趣

sentences.en: So people will be selfless
sentences.zh: 好让人们变得无私

sentences.en: It's Christmas time
sentences.zh: 圣诞节到了

sentences.en: Merry Christmas, Maggie
sentences.zh: 圣诞快乐，玛吉

sentences.en: Merry Christmas, Adam
sentences.zh: 圣诞快乐，亚当

sentences.en: Merry Christmas, Santa
sentences.zh: 圣诞快乐，圣诞老人

sentences.en: Merry Christmas, listeners
sentences.zh: 圣诞快乐，听众朋友们

sentences.en: I'm watching you
sentences.zh: 我看着你呢

sentences.en: That was fantastic, Adam
sentences.zh: 太棒了，亚当

sentences.en: Well, thank you so much
sentences.zh: 非常感谢

sentences.en: I clearly stand corrected
sentences.zh: 我显然收回刚才的话

sentences.en: For all you kids out there
sentences.zh: 所有的孩子们

sentences.en: You clearly heard two different voices
sentences.zh: 你们显然听到了两个不同的声音

sentences.en: Santa is on the episode, on tape
sentences.zh: 圣诞老人在这期节目里，有录音为证

sentences.en: So Santa Claus exists
sentences.zh: 所以圣诞老人是存在的

sentences.en: And I was wrong
sentences.zh: 而我错了

sentences.en: That's right
sentences.zh: 没准

sentences.en: I'm glad that you are a big enough man to admit that
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你是个拿得起放得下的大男人，能承认这一点

sentences.en: Adam, thank you so much for joining me
sentences.zh: 亚当，非常感谢你参加我们的节目

sentences.en: Thanks for having me
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来
